title: Pinto Coat Colors
short_description: Let's sort out the different pinto patterns. As in the other quizzes, the idea is simple: look at the photo and choose the correct answer. Even if you learn nothing, at least you'll see some beautiful horses.
intro: Let's sort out the different pinto patterns. As in the other quizzes, the idea is simple: look at the photo and choose the correct answer. Even if you learn nothing, at least you'll see some beautiful horses.
questionImagesAlt: Photo of a horse for identifying its pinto pattern

questions.question: What coat color and pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Frame overo is a pinto pattern in which white patches with crisp, irregular edges appear mainly on the sides of the body and usually do not cross the topline, creating the impression that the dark color is enclosed by a white “frame.” The face often has broad white markings, while the legs frequently remain dark.

questions.question: What coat color and pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Sabino is a pinto pattern in which white markings begin on the legs and face—a blaze may extend from the forelock to the lower jaw—and spread onto the belly and sides. Sabino markings typically have irregular, ragged, or roaned edges, with numerous white hairs mixed into the base coat.

questions.question: What coat color and pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Splashed white is a pinto pattern that makes the horse look as though its lower body has been dipped in white paint. It features large white markings with crisp, smooth edges that begin on the legs and underside, extend onto the head, and are often accompanied by blue eyes.

questions.question: What coat color and pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Tobiano is a pinto pattern in which large white patches with crisp, usually smooth edges cross the topline and extend down the sides. The legs are usually white, the head generally remains dark with ordinary facial markings such as a blaze, and the tail is often two-colored.
